snippet.title: How to use Zencoaching | Coaching Defintions & FAQS | Thank you for 10K!
snippet.description:
Free/$5/$10 coaches are available on discord. 

Zen Socials
Discord: https://discord.gg/cUtyjfz   (Contact FREE or $5/$10 Coaches HERE)
Twitch: https://www.twitch.tv/zencoaching
Twitter: @ZenCoachingLol

Elsa Socials 
Twitch: https://www.twitch.tv/elsagamingtv/videos
Instagram: @elsagamingtv



I do not own the music used. 
Link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxHv0jCrX_k

Definitions: 
Tethering – Standing around the maximum range of an opponent’s abilities or harassing under tower 
 
Clash – The line at which both minion waves meet. This line usually indicates which way the wave may push. If the clash is closer to your side and the minions are even in count, the wave will passively push towards the opposing side. This is because of the next reinforcing wave
Slow Push – Last hitting the waves and slowly pushing the wave to eventually lead to a wave build-up

30% for 30% - Trading 30% of your HP, for 30% of the enemies HP either leading to a benefit in the lane or a misplay. You will often see Zen tell people that they can or cannot take a 30 for 30 trade here. 

Right pocket / Left pocket – The lanes are divided by an invisible grid and pockets are small spaces that players will retain in order to play the lane correctly. Pockets are important for trading. 
Trade Pocket & Trade Minion – Trade Pocket is the pocket that you will take in relation to your minions that the enemy will last hit. The minion that you will trade on is called the trade minion. Trade pockets change relative to trade minions. 

Crashing – Crashing is simply throwing the minion wave under the enemy’s tower. Crashing can be done to either take a recall, establish or deny vision, set up a dive or assist your team around the map. 

Building – Building a wave is essentially last hitting a slow push so two or three waves build up. Building waves usually happen when you want to take an advantageous recall timing, again, establish or deny vision, set up a dive inside of a huge pool of minions in order to not take disadvantages trades. 

Leveling the wave – Leveling the wave is done when you are attempting to establish a freeze. When the wave is coming into you, you want to thin it to the point where you can have it constantly lock with your next incoming wave in order to retain a longer freeze.

Using HP/Mana as a resource – Using your HP & Mana as a resource can be done when you are at a lane disadvantage and you throw your entire mana pool or take a disadvantage trade in order to retain a better lane state in the future. This will put you at a small opening against the enemy jungler, however, protects you from future ganks. This is a very complex topic and It will be elaborated further in the videos. 

First response – First response is pretty much getting to the wave first in order to manipulate it at level 1. First response is also tempo-based, reaching the fight first, reaching the lane first, establishing vision control first, etc. 

Bounce on “3” or Bounce on “4” – Bouncing on waves 3 means pushing wave 1 and wave 2 and 3 will come back into your side of the lane. Bounces on 4 are more frequent. This means that you will push wave 1, push on wave 2, wave 3 will act as a buffer (which we will go into In a second) and wave 4 will bounce back. This grants you safety from the jungler and the lane opponent while setting yourself up for a kill or simply setting up your own jungler for a gank opening. 

Buffer – The buffer wave will be the wave that will come before the bounce. If you push wave A, B, and C – wave “D” will buffer and wave E and F will be played around your angle

Dance - Dancing is rapid movements back and forth. These changes relative to the lane opponent and will be further discussed in the videos.
